explanation: The plan uses a story-to-film pipeline for a single scripted talking head, relying on generated clip speech rather than a guaranteed exact voice track and a dedicated talking-photo tool. It also assumes film finishing will add accurate timed captions, and several pipeline steps omit required upstream inputs. Nothing was run, so the record establishes non-delivery, not an observed visual or speech-quality failure.
better_chain: image (create a fictional adult woman in her 30s, selfie-framed at home, vertical 9:16) → voice (speak the supplied English script exactly in a friendly neutral female voice, paced to approximately 8 seconds) → talking-photo (animate the presenter speaking that audio) → captions (transcribe and time the spoken English) → gate (verify exact caption wording, complete speech, visible speaking, duration, and vertical format)

steps.issue: A story stage is unnecessary for one continuous talking-camera shot with an already supplied script.
An asset-bank stage adds unnecessary indirection; one image generation can establish the fictional presenter and home setting.
The screenplay tool requires both story and bank, but only assets.json is wired in. Rewriting the supplied script into a screenplay is also unnecessary.
The keyframes stage requires the screenplay and asset bank, but receives only screenplay.json, leaving presenter identity and setting continuity dependent on implicit state.

Generated clip speech is not the right route for guaranteed exact dialogue and synchronized speaking. Use talking-photo with an explicit voice track; the proposed clips call also omits its required screenplay input.
Film finishing has no documented guarantee of exact timed captions or disclosure overlays. Use the dedicated captions tool for speech captions, and text-overlay if a disclosure is desired.

missing: An explicit exact-script voice track, a talking-photo step driven by that track, and a dedicated timed-caption step with verification. All planned steps also remained unexecuted.
